slides.title: Multilayer + multiplex networks
slides.body:
**Multilayer networks**: real systems often have **multiple types** of connections simultaneously. Single-layer (monoplex) abstractions discard crucial structure.

**Boccaletti + Bianconi + Criado + del Genio + Gómez-Gardeñes + Romance + Sendiña-Nadal + Wang + Zanin (2014 Physics Reports *The structure + dynamics of multilayer networks*)** — canonical 122-page review; >5,000 citations.

**Terminology**:
- **Multiplex**: same node set across layers (e.g. same people on Facebook + Twitter + LinkedIn); each layer has different edge type.
- **Interconnected / interlayer networks**: distinct node sets per layer + interlayer edges (e.g. air + rail transport networks coupled at transfer stations).
- **Multidimensional networks**: edges labeled by 'aspects' (time, type, layer).
- **Multislice / temporal networks**: layers = time snapshots (special case).

**Tensor formalism** (de Domenico + Solé-Ribalta + Cozzo + Kivelä + Moreno + Porter + Gómez + Arenas 2013 PRX *Mathematical formulation of multilayer networks*): generalize adjacency matrix A_ij to fourth-order tensor M^{αβ}_{ij} where α, β index layers + i, j index nodes within layers. Captures all interlayer + intralayer edges in unified algebra. Eigenvalues + eigenvectors of supra-adjacency / supra-Laplacian matrices generalize spectral methods.

**Supra-adjacency matrix**: stack each layer + connect corresponding nodes across layers with interlayer couplings. (n·L) × (n·L) matrix for n nodes + L layers.

**Multiplex centrality**: PageRank, eigenvector centrality generalize but care needed — different layer weights yield different rankings; tensor formulations give principled approaches (de Domenico + Solé-Ribalta + Omodei + Gómez + Arenas 2015).

**Multiplex percolation** (Buldyrev + Parshani + Paul + Stanley + Havlin 2010 Nature *Catastrophic cascade of failures in interdependent networks*): coupled networks (power grid + Internet) show **discontinuous (first-order) percolation transition** vs continuous (second-order) for single networks — small fraction of failures triggers catastrophic collapse. Inspired by 2003 Italy blackout (power grid failure cascaded via SCADA Internet failure). One of the most-cited network-science papers.

**Layer-coupling effects**:
- **Spreading on multiplex** (Cozzo + Banos + Meloni + Moreno 2013): a disease on layer A + an awareness/immunization process on layer B couple; awareness suppresses spreading.
- **Multiplex synchronization**: stability + thresholds depend on interlayer coupling strength.
- **Multilayer communities** (Mucha + Richardson + Macon + Porter + Onnela 2010 Science): generalized modularity Q with interlayer coupling parameter ω; reveals consistent vs layer-specific groups.

**Real multilayer datasets**:
- **Multimodal transport** (air + rail + road).
- **Multispecies ecological** (predation + competition + mutualism).
- **Multi-omics biology** (gene-gene + protein-protein + metabolic).
- **Brain multiplex** (Battiston + Nicosia + Chavez + Latora 2017): structural + functional layers.
- **Social multiplex**: Facebook + Twitter + LinkedIn same users.

**Software**: pymnet (Kivelä), multiNetX, MuxViz (de Domenico), igraph + tensorly for tensor analysis.

slides.title: Temporal networks: when edges have timestamps
slides.body:
**Temporal networks** (Petter Holme + Jari Saramäki 2012 Physics Reports *Temporal networks*; 2019 book): edges are time-stamped events rather than static links. Crucial for analyzing real systems where **timing + causality matter**.

**Examples**:
- **Email + phone-call networks**: each communication = timestamped edge.
- **Sexual contact networks**: pivotal for HIV/STI modeling.
- **Face-to-face proximity** (SocioPatterns RFID datasets at conferences, schools, hospitals; Cattuto + Van den Broeck + Barrat + Colizza + Pinton + Vespignani 2010).
- **Citation networks** (asymmetric in time).
- **Neuronal spike trains** (functional connectivity in time).
- **Trade + financial transactions**.
- **Mobile-phone CDR data** (Karsai + Kivelä + Pan + Kaski + Kertész + Barabási + Saramäki 2011): burstiness, temporal correlations.
- **Twitter retweet cascades**.

**Time-respecting paths** (Kempe + Kleinberg + Kumar 2000): a sequence of edges (i_0, i_1, t_0), (i_1, i_2, t_1), ... with t_0 ≤ t_1 ≤ ... — respects causality. Reachability is **asymmetric** + path lengths between same pair may differ in different directions. Static aggregation **destroys** this asymmetry.

**Temporal motifs** (Paranjape + Benson + Leskovec 2017): generalize Milo-Alon network motifs to temporal subgraphs with edge orderings. Different motif distributions in: email vs trust networks vs face-to-face. Captures dynamical signatures.

**Inter-event time distributions** (Barabási 2005 Nature *The origin of bursts + heavy tails in human dynamics*): time between consecutive activities of an individual follows **heavy-tailed** distribution (~ power law or stretched exponential), not exponential as Poisson processes assume. Bursts of activity separated by long quiet periods. Universal in human behavior — email, calls, web browsing.

**Effect on spreading**:
- **Burstiness slows spreading** in many regimes (Karsai et al. 2011): long quiet periods between bursts delay outbreaks.
- But heavy-tailed inter-event times can also create explosive cascades when bursts coincide.
- **Temporal correlations** (vs random shuffling of timestamps) usually slow spreading + epidemics, but the effect is system-specific.

**Temporal communities + dynamical groups**:
- **Mucha + Richardson + Macon + Porter + Onnela (2010 Science)**: generalized modularity on temporal multilayer networks with interlayer coupling ω — communities consistent over time vs short-lived.
- **Sliding-window analysis**: simpler but reveals merging, splitting, birth, death of communities (Palla + Barabási + Vicsek 2007 Nature).
- **DSBM** (dynamic stochastic block model).

**Inference of dynamics + temporal centrality**:
- **Temporal PageRank, temporal betweenness**: rank nodes by their role in time-respecting paths.
- **Tie strength inference**: Onnela 2007 mobile-phone data showed weak ties are crucial for global connectivity but strong ties locally.

**Modern + open**:
- **Online streaming** algorithms for huge dynamic graphs.
- **Temporal graph neural networks** (TGN — Rossi et al. 2020; TGAT, DyRep): incorporate time into GNN message passing.
- **Continuous-time vs discrete-time formulations**.
- **Granger / transfer-entropy causality on temporal networks**.

**Software**: pathpy (Scholtes), teneto, TGL (Temporal Graph Library), Tigramite for causal discovery.

slides.title: Higher-order interactions: simplicial complexes, hypergraphs + TDA
slides.body:
**Beyond pairwise edges**: many real interactions involve **more than two entities** simultaneously — co-authorship of papers (3+ authors), multi-party conversations, protein complexes, multi-gene transcription, ecological mutualism among multiple species. Edges miss these higher-order interactions.

**Hypergraphs** (Berge 1973 *Graphs + Hypergraphs*): generalize edges to **hyperedges** containing any number of nodes. Adjacency tensor of order = max hyperedge size. Modern analytical tools: hypergraph spectral theory, hypergraph Laplacian, hypergraph clustering.

**Simplicial complexes** (algebraic topology): collection of simplices closed under taking faces. A 2-simplex (triangle) implies all three of its edges (1-simplices) + vertices (0-simplices) are included. **Boundary operators** ∂_k: C_k → C_(k-1) satisfy ∂² = 0; homology H_k = ker(∂_k) / im(∂_(k+1)) measures k-dimensional holes.

**Battiston + Cencetti + Iacopini + Latora + Lucas + Patania + Young + Petri (2020 Physics Reports *Networks beyond pairwise interactions*)**: canonical review of higher-order network science. Two key insights:
- **Higher-order dynamics differ qualitatively** from pairwise approximations: explosive synchronization, bistability, abrupt transitions, qualitatively new collective behaviors.
- **Many real datasets contain higher-order interactions** that monoplex graphs cannot represent — co-authorship is best modeled as hyperedges.

**Examples of higher-order phenomena**:
- **Simplicial Kuramoto** (Millán + Restrepo + Torres 2020): higher-order coupling produces explosive synchronization + multistability.
- **Hypergraph epidemics** (Iacopini + Petri + Barrat + Latora 2019 Nature Communications): contagion via triangles + hyperedges shows abrupt transitions vs gradual onset on pairwise networks.
- **Hypergraph consensus, voter models, evolutionary games**: novel dynamics.

**Topological Data Analysis (TDA)** (Gunnar Carlsson 2009 *Topology + data*; >7,000 citations) — uses algebraic topology to summarize shape of data.

**Persistent homology**: build a sequence of simplicial complexes from data (e.g. **Vietoris-Rips complex** with growing radius). Track when homology classes (connected components, loops, voids) appear + disappear. **Persistence diagrams** + **barcodes** summarize features that persist across scales. Robust to noise.

**Applications of TDA + persistent homology**:
- **Image + 3D shape analysis**.
- **Protein structure** (binding pockets, cavities).
- **Brain networks** (Sizemore + Phillips-Cremins + Ghrist + Bassett 2019; loops + cavities in functional brain networks correlate with cognition).
- **Cosmic web** (large-scale structure of universe).
- **Time-series analysis** (sliding-window TDA).
- **Genomics**: persistence of recombination events.
- **Materials science**: detecting defect structures.

**Software**: GUDHI (Inria; reference C++/Python), Ripser (fast persistent homology), giotto-tda, scikit-tda, HyperNetX (LBNL hypergraphs).

**Modern + open**:
- **Hypergraph neural networks** (Feng + You + Zhang + Ji + Gao 2019; HGNN, HyperGCN): GNNs generalized to hyperedges.
- **Simplicial neural networks** (Bunch + You + Carlsson + Hamilton 2020).
- **Cellular complexes + cell complexes** as generalization.
- **Topological deep learning** (Hajij + Zamzmi + Papamarkou + Maroulas + Cai + Ramamurthy + Birdal + Wang 2022 review): emerging field at the intersection of TDA + ML.
- **Graph + simplicial GNNs in molecular property prediction, materials discovery**.

Higher-order representations promise to be as transformative as the move from lattices to networks in the 2000s.

question.question: Derive supra-adjacency + cascade fragility on interdependent networks
question.goal: Sketch why coupled networks (Buldyrev et al. 2010) have first-order percolation transition.

steps.prompt: Two coupled networks A + B; each node in A is paired to one in B. A node functions only if both its copy in A + its copy in B are in their respective giant components. Set up the recursion.

acceptedAnswers: fraction g_A of A is in giant; require corresponding B-nodes also in giant

hints: Iterate: remove failed nodes in A → some B-counterparts fail → more A fails.
steps.reveal: Iterative cascade: remove fraction (1-p) of A's nodes; compute giant component of remaining; identify corresponding B-nodes whose A-partner failed → remove those from B; recompute B's giant; iterate. Mutual giant = fixed point.

steps.prompt: Single ER network: continuous transition at p_c = 1/⟨k⟩. What happens for two coupled ER networks?

acceptedAnswers: first-order discontinuous transition at p_c higher than single-network

hints: Cascade amplifies failures; mutual giant collapses abruptly.
steps.reveal: Buldyrev et al. 2010 Nature: for two coupled ER networks with mean degree ⟨k⟩, the mutual giant component undergoes a **first-order (discontinuous) phase transition** at p_c ≈ 2.4554/⟨k⟩ — significantly higher than single-network p_c = 1/⟨k⟩. At p_c the giant component drops abruptly to zero. Small additional damage causes catastrophic cascade. Inspired by 2003 Italy blackout (power grid + Internet SCADA coupling).

steps.prompt: What's the implication for real-world critical infrastructure?

acceptedAnswers: design for cascade resilience; avoid tight one-to-one coupling; build redundancy

hints: Reduce dependency degree; randomize coupling; redundant paths.
steps.reveal: Engineering implications: (1) reduce tight one-to-one interlayer coupling; (2) introduce multiple redundant interlayer dependencies; (3) island networks to limit cascade reach; (4) heterogeneous coupling (Parshani + Buldyrev + Havlin 2010) — coupling fraction q matters: low q → continuous; high q → discontinuous; (5) include sequential repair dynamics. Post-2010 literature: coupled-network resilience for power grids, transportation + financial systems (Battiston DebtRank, post-2008 financial-stability work).

steps.prompt: How does this connect to multilayer-modularity community detection (Mucha 2010)?

acceptedAnswers: same supra-Laplacian / supra-adjacency framework; interlayer coupling ω

steps.reveal: Mucha + Richardson + Macon + Porter + Onnela (2010 Science) used **supra-adjacency** + generalized modularity to detect communities in multilayer + temporal networks with interlayer coupling parameter ω. Same algebra (tensor / supra-matrices) underlies both percolation + community-detection on multilayer networks. de Domenico + Solé-Ribalta + Cozzo + Kivelä + Moreno + Porter + Gómez + Arenas (2013 PRX) systematized the tensor formalism.

question.question: Why are higher-order networks (hypergraphs, simplicial complexes) considered the next frontier of network science?
options: Battiston + Cencetti + Iacopini + Latora + Lucas + Patania + Young + Petri (2020 Physics Reports *Networks beyond pairwise interactions*) review showed that **higher-order interactions** (3-body, 4-body, group interactions modeled as hyperedges or simplices) cannot be reduced to pairwise edges without losing essential structure. Real systems with higher-order structure: co-authorship (groups of n authors collaborating), protein complexes (multi-subunit assemblies), multi-party social conversations, ecological mutualism, neural assemblies, gene-regulation triplets. Pairwise approximations miss these. Iacopini + Petri + Barrat + Latora (2019 Nature Communications) showed contagion on hypergraphs displays **abrupt transitions, bistability, hysteresis** absent from pairwise SIS — qualitatively different dynamics. Simplicial Kuramoto (Millán + Restrepo + Torres 2020) shows explosive synchronization. Topological data analysis (Carlsson 2009; >7,000 citations) uses persistent homology to detect loops + voids in data via simplicial complexes — applied to brain networks (Sizemore + Bassett 2019), cosmic web, materials, protein structures. Software: GUDHI, Ripser, HyperNetX. Modern: hypergraph neural networks (HGNN, HyperGCN), simplicial neural networks (Bunch et al. 2020), topological deep learning (Hajij et al. 2022). Higher-order representations promise to be as transformative as the move from lattices to networks in the 2000s — capturing structure ML on flat graphs cannot.
question.explanation: Battiston et al (2020 Physics Reports) showed higher-order interactions (hyperedges, simplices) capture multi-body structure pairwise edges miss. Co-authorship, protein complexes, multi-party conversations. Iacopini et al (2019 Nature Comms) showed contagion on hypergraphs shows abrupt transitions + bistability absent from pairwise SIS. TDA + persistent homology (Carlsson 2009) detects loops + voids via simplicial complexes. Modern hypergraph + simplicial neural networks (Bunch, Hajij 2022 topological DL) extend GNNs.

Iacopini et al (2019 Nature Comms) showed hypergraph contagion has abrupt + bistable transitions; Millán et al (2020) showed explosive synchronization. TDA (Carlsson 2009) detects loops/voids via persistent homology — applied to brain (Sizemore-Bassett), cosmic web. Hypergraph + simplicial neural networks + topological DL (Hajij 2022) are frontier ML.

How would you simulate the cascade dynamics + verify against the actual 2003 timeline? What design recommendations follow (redundancy, partial coupling, island-mode operation)? Connect to Battiston + DebtRank (2012) for financial cascades + the post-2010 critical-infrastructure literature. What modern frameworks (HyperNetX, multinetx) would you use?

question.question: Write the supra-adjacency block structure for two coupled networks A + B with interlayer coupling C and intralayer adjacencies A^(1) and A^(2).
acceptedAnswers: supra-A = block matrix with A^(1) and A^(2) on diagonal + C off-diagonal
question.hint: Block matrix: intralayer on diagonal blocks, interlayer on off-diagonal.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain why multilayer, temporal + higher-order networks are essential frontiers of network science.
question.rubric: Mentions: Single-layer static pairwise graphs miss critical structure. Multilayer / multiplex networks (Boccaletti review 2014; de Domenico tensor formalism 2013 PRX) handle multiple edge types simultaneously; Buldyrev + Parshani + Paul + Stanley + Havlin (2010 Nature) showed interdependent networks have first-order percolation transitions — catastrophic cascades inspired by 2003 Italy blackout; Mucha (2010 Science) generalized modularity to multilayer + temporal communities. Temporal networks (Holme + Saramäki 2012 Physics Reports) — edges have timestamps, time-respecting paths matter, burstiness (Barabási 2005) reshapes spreading; temporal motifs (Paranjape + Benson + Leskovec 2017); SocioPatterns datasets. Higher-order (Battiston et al 2020 Physics Reports): hyperedges + simplicial complexes capture multi-body interactions impossible to express pairwise; hypergraph contagion (Iacopini 2019 Nature Comms) shows abrupt + bistable transitions; simplicial Kuramoto, explosive sync. Topological data analysis (Carlsson 2009) via persistent homology detects loops + voids. Modern ML: hypergraph GNNs, simplicial neural networks, topological deep learning (Hajij 2022). Together they're as transformative as the move from lattices to networks in the 2000s.
